analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily (13.11.2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 fell 35bps to 7592 (+11% YTD) on lower volumes. SOX was basically unchanged and attention was on Nvidia, which closed -4% after a management change (Jensen resignation) and rumours the note describes as a third affair.

Nvidia: GS compares the management transition to Apple's situation. It expects a measured direct impact on Nvidia's financials and earnings power over the next 12-18 months, given a 12-24 month backlog and order book and a defined 2-3 year product roadmap already in execution. The stock's multiple is expected to take a greater hit because of uncertainty. Buy rating retained on positive risk/reward.
Cross-asset levels: US 10yr yield 5.13%, US dollar near an 18-month high (EUR/USD 1.106), Brent $96, Gold $3891, Bitcoin $69k.
Microsoft has a global outage affecting Outlook and Teams. The company ruled out a cyberattack and said it is working to address the issue. The fix is not going as expected.
Meta's agent Muse can now place calls on behalf of users. The feature is available to paid subscribers.
Middle East: the US military has reportedly warned Israel to prepare for a resumption of the war in Iran, days after Trump said renewed attacks on Iran were 'highly unlikely'.

US debt: the government started fiscal 2027 with a $404bn October budget deficit, a record for the month and up $120bn (42% y/y). Agriculture, military and interest drove spending. Interest was $115bn in October (+11%) against receipts of $369bn (-9% y/y).

GS 2027 macro outlook: global growth of +2.8% in 2027 vs +2.7% in 2026, as lower energy prices and strong AI capex outweigh tighter financial conditions and more neutral fiscal policy. Risks are to the downside (Iran, higher deficits, lower AI capex). GS expects 2 Fed hikes and 1 ECB hike from today, then cuts later in 2027.

GS 2027 equities outlook: S&P 500 target 8700 (+14%). US EPS growth is expected to slow from 32% to 17%, so investors will seek companies that can sustain growth. Equities have de-rated sharply, and GS expects further gains with high volatility. It favours growth balanced with selective defensives and beneficiaries of lower bond yields, and sees long-duration growth companies as increasingly valuable as growth slows.

GS 2027 markets outlook themes: maturing market cycle, AI investment impulse peaks, energy risk premium, bonds regaining macro and hedging value, a more cyclical dollar, Europe/UK shifts, stress of financing the boom, EM resilience, growth risks and tail hedges.

Semis: GS thinks the current drawdown is overdone. 35 GW of 2027 deployments are largely in progress and carry low execution risk. NVDA and AVGO are at very attractive entry points, and AMAT and LRCX are particularly compelling.

US capex: GS economist sees 2026 capex up 11% and forecasts real business fixed investment growth of 8% in 2027. AI stays the dominant driver, but official statistics will show less impact than company spending data because most equipment is imported. Midterm results pose modest risk to AI investment. Manufacturing facility spending is expected to decline while energy investment rises.

Stat of the Day: the US equity market is still the most expensive but has moderated from near its 100th percentile over 20 years to a P/E of 18.5x. Asia and EM trade well below their historical average P/E. Overall P/E ratios are around their 35-year average, and PEG ratios show a similar pattern.
Chart of the Day: the valuation premium of the largest US companies has narrowed.
